If you need to know where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi, start at Hiking Outdoor Gear Hub in Mountain Mall on Thika Road (3rd Floor, Shop D39). You can try quality thrifted and new boots from Lowa, Keen and Quechua with your own hiking socks on, or order online and pay with M-Pesa or cash on delivery.

A boot that pinches in the shop will hurt far more on the loose ash below Mt Longonot's rim or in the black-cotton mud of a short-rains morning. Below we cover where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi, which type of boot suits Kenyan trails, a six-step fit routine, what to look for on a pre-owned pair, the mistakes people make most often, and how to make boots last.

Quick Facts

  • Where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi: Mountain Mall, 3rd Floor, Shop D39, Thika Road, close to Kasarani, Garden Estate and Thome
  • Shop hours: Monday–Friday 8:30am–6:00pm, Saturday 9:00am–2:00pm, Sunday by appointment
  • Online orders: hikingoutdoorhub.com, paid by M-Pesa or cash on delivery
  • Best all-round type for Kenya: a mid-cut waterproof boot with a deep, lugged rubber sole
  • Toe room: roughly a thumb's width (1–1.5 cm) between your longest toe and the front of the boot
  • Best time to try boots on: late afternoon, wearing the socks you hike in

Which Type of Hiking Boot Suits Kenyan Trails?

A mid-cut waterproof boot suits most Kenyan hikers. It covers the ankle bone on loose scree, keeps feet dry through both rainy seasons and grips on muddy forest paths, which describes almost every trail within a day of Nairobi.

Decide on the type before you decide where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi, because the type narrows the shelf quickly. Use this as a starting point:

Boot typeBest forKenyan examples
Low-cut hiking shoeDry, well-made paths and light daypacksKarura Forest, Oloolua Nature Trail
Mid-cut hiking bootMost day hikes: mud, loose rock, steep descentsNgong Hills, Mt Longonot, Ol Donyo Sabuk, Elephant Hill
Stiff high-cut trekking bootMulti-day treks, heavy packs, cold and wet high groundMt Kenya, the Aberdares moorland, Kilimanjaro

Our longer article on hiking boots for Kenyan trails goes deeper into leather versus fabric uppers, sole stiffness and membranes. If you mostly do light, dry routes and like a fast pace, a low shoe can be enough; our post on Salomon hiking shoes explains where light footwear works and where it does not.

Do you need waterproof hiking boots in Kenya?

Waterproof boots earn their place in Kenya because the long rains (roughly March to May) and short rains (roughly October to December) turn red soil into slick mud. The Kenya Meteorological Department's October–December seasonal outlook pointed to a wetter-than-usual short-rains season for Nairobi, with rain running into January. If you are working out where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi during October or November, a waterproof pair is the safer bet.

In the hot, dry months a non-waterproof boot breathes better and dries faster after a river crossing. For a full comparison of membranes and what keeps water out longest, see our post on waterproof hiking boots in Nairobi. On very muddy routes, pair any boot with waterproof leg gaiters so water and grit cannot get in over the collar.

How Should Hiking Boots Fit?

Hiking boots should hold your heel and midfoot snugly while leaving your toes free to wiggle, with about a thumb's width in front of the longest toe. On a slope, your toes should never touch the front, and your heel should lift only slightly.

Run through these six checks with every pair, in this order. They take about ten minutes, save weeks of blisters, and work wherever you settle on where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi:

  1. Shop late in the day. Feet swell a little by afternoon, much as they do a few hours into a hike.
  2. Wear your hiking socks. A thick cushioned sock can take up half a size compared with a thin office sock.
  3. Do the finger test before lacing. Slide your foot forward until your toes touch the front; one finger should fit behind your heel.
  4. Lace firmly and walk for five minutes, including stairs. A flight of stairs is a fair stand-in for a rocky path.
  5. Test a descent. Walk down a ramp or step and check that your toes stay clear of the front of the boot.
  6. Try both feet. Most people have one foot slightly larger, and the boot must fit that one.

If one pair passes all six checks and another fails one, take the pair that passes, whatever the colour. That rule matters more than brand loyalty when you decide where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi.

What size hiking boots should I buy?

Buy the size that fits your longer foot with hiking socks on, which for many people is half a size above their everyday shoes. Measure your foot length in centimetres, standing, and compare it with each brand's chart, since sizing differs between brands. The insole test is the tie-breaker: pull the insole out, stand on it, and check there is about a thumb's width of insole beyond your longest toe.

Do women need women's hiking boots?

Many women find women's-specific boots fit better because they are built on a narrower last, with a slimmer heel and lower volume over the instep. Some women with wider feet are comfortable in men's models, so try both. Are Second-Hand Hiking Boots Worth Buying in Nairobi?

Second-hand hiking boots are worth buying when the tread, midsole and upper still have plenty of life left. A well-made pre-owned boot from a serious outdoor brand often outlasts a cheap new pair, and costs a fraction of its original price.

For many people researching where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi, quality thrifted boots are what make a proper Gore-Tex pair affordable at all. The point is to judge each pair on its condition, not its age or its logo. Use this table whenever you pick up a pre-owned boot, in our shop or anywhere else:

Part of the bootWhat to look for when buyingWalk away if
TreadDeep, sharp lugs at the heel and toeLugs are worn smooth or rounded
MidsoleFirm, even foam that springs back under a thumb pressDeep cracks, crumbling, or a flat, dead feel
Sole bondSole attached all the way round when you flex the bootA gap opens at the toe or heel
Heel counterFirm cup at the back of the heelIt folds in easily when squeezed
LiningSmooth inside the heel and around the ankleWorn-through lining that could rub
Upper and eyeletsNo splits; every hook and eyelet secureCracked leather or torn stitching at the flex point

Why can an old, unworn boot still fall apart?

An unworn boot can still fail because some polyurethane (PU) midsoles break down chemically over time, a process called hydrolysis. Boot maker Meindl explains in its guide to sole hydrolysis that long storage without flexing, and storing boots damp, are the main causes, and the result is a sole that crumbles or separates.

So a pair that looks almost new but has a crumbly midsole is not a bargain. Whichever way you answer where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi, bend every boot hard at the forefoot and press the midsole with your thumb before you pay. Boots that have been walked in regularly are often in better shape than boots that sat in a box for years.

Pro Tips: Where to Buy Hiking Boots in Nairobi Without Regrets

  • Bring your socks: the exact pair you plan to hike in, not new ones.
  • Bring your insoles: if you use custom or after-market insoles, fit the boot with them in.
  • Know your foot length: measure in centimetres at home, standing, both feet.
  • Name your trails: tell us whether you hike Karura, Longonot or Mt Kenya; the right stiffness differs.
  • Flex every boot: look for gaps between sole and upper at the toe and heel.
  • Allow break-in time: buy at least two weeks before a big hike, not the Friday before.

Common Mistakes When Choosing Where to Buy Hiking Boots in Nairobi

The commonest mistake when working out where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi is buying without trying boots on, closely followed by buying for looks rather than fit. Both are easy to avoid if you plan the purchase rather than squeezing it into a lunch break.

Buying a size that fits only in the shop

A boot that feels "just right" with thin socks at 10am will feel tight at 2pm on a hot descent. Whatever you decide about where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi, fit with hiking socks, late in the day, and if you are between sizes, go for the larger one and fine-tune with lacing or a thicker sock.

Choosing a mountaineering boot for day hikes

Very stiff, heavy boots are built for crampons and heavy loads, so ask about weight and flex when you weigh up where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi. On Ngong Hills or Ol Donyo Sabuk they mostly add weight and slow your feet down. A flexible mid-cut boot is the better buy unless Mt Kenya or Kilimanjaro is on your calendar; our hiking gear checklist for Kenya matches footwear to each type of hike.

Skipping socks in the budget

Cotton socks hold sweat and cause blisters even in a perfect boot, so budget for socks while you sort out where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi. A pair of merino wool hiking socks manages moisture and cushions the ball of the foot. Our post on hiking socks in Nairobi explains weights and lengths.

How Do You Break In and Care for Hiking Boots in Nairobi?

Once you have settled where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi, break the boots in by wearing them indoors, then on short walks, over one to two weeks before a long hike. After every outing, knock off the mud, rinse with clean water and dry them slowly at room temperature.

How long does it take to break in hiking boots?

Most modern fabric and synthetic boots need only a few days of short walks. Stiff full-grain leather boots can take two weeks or more. Either way, the test is a real hill: a half-day on Ngong Hills or the steep, dusty descent on Mt Longonot will show any hot spot before it becomes a blister on a bigger trip.

Our Mt Longonot hike guide describes that descent, and the best day hikes near Nairobi round-up lists gentler first outings for new boots.

How should you clean and store hiking boots?

Clean boots with a soft brush and plain water, take the insoles out and stuff the boots with newspaper to draw out moisture. Never dry them beside a jiko, a campfire or in strong direct sun; heat cracks leather and weakens the glue that holds the sole.

Re-proof leather with a wax made for boots, and fabric boots with a spray-on treatment once water stops beading on the surface. Store them dry and somewhere airy, not sealed in a bag at the back of a cupboard, and wear them every few weeks so the midsole keeps flexing between big trips.

Dust is the other enemy. Whether you sorted out where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi online or in person, brush fine red dust off after dry-season hikes, because it dries out leather. With the short rains here, pair clean boots with a good shell from our guide to rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi on a budget?

The cheapest sensible answer to where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi on a budget is a shop selling quality thrifted outdoor gear. Hiking Outdoor Gear Hub at Mountain Mall on Thika Road stocks pre-owned and new boots from brands such as Lowa, Keen and Quechua, so you can get a waterproof, supportive pair for well under the price of the same boot new.

Can I just hike in sneakers?

Sneakers work on short, dry, well-made paths such as Karura Forest, but they lack the grip, ankle support and toe protection that loose or muddy trails need. On Ngong Hills, Mt Longonot or any hike during the rains, hiking boots or trail shoes with a deep lugged sole are far safer and more comfortable.

Should hiking boots be a size bigger than my normal shoes?

Hiking boots are often half a size bigger than everyday shoes because you wear thicker socks and your feet swell on long walks. The right size leaves about a thumb's width in front of the longest toe while holding the heel firmly. Always fit hiking boots to your larger foot, with your hiking socks on.

How long do hiking boots last?

Hiking boots usually last several hundred kilometres of trail, depending on weight, terrain, materials and care. Replace them when the tread is worn smooth, the midsole feels flat or crumbly, the sole starts to separate, or the boots let water in even after re-proofing. Regular wear and dry storage help boots last longer.

What boots are best for climbing Mt Kenya?

Mid- or high-cut waterproof boots with a fairly stiff sole and good ankle support are best for Mt Kenya. Routes cross bog, scree and freezing ground above 4,000 m, so choose a pair with room for thick socks and break it in well, since fit matters more than the shop when you weigh up where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi. Our Mt Kenya hiking guide covers the routes themselves.

Final Thoughts

Nobody else's feet can tell you whether a boot fits, which is why the honest answer to where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi is any place that lets you try several pairs properly. Pick a mid-cut waterproof boot for most Kenyan trails, fit it to your larger foot with hiking socks, and flex every pre-owned pair before paying.
